name: Ulrich Körner

summary.text: Ulrich Körner became Group CEO of Credit Suisse on 1 August 2022, succeeding Thomas Gottstein, after rejoining the bank in April 2021 to head asset management following eleven years at UBS. He was chief executive when, on 19 March 2023, the Swiss authorities arranged Credit Suisse's takeover by UBS and the write-down of its AT1 capital.

facts.claim: Credit Suisse announced on 27 July 2022 that Ulrich Körner would succeed Thomas Gottstein as Group CEO effective 1 August 2022, alongside a comprehensive strategic review.
facts.quote: according to a statement issued by Credit Suisse on 27 July 2022

facts.claim: Körner rejoined Credit Suisse in April 2021 to lead asset management after eleven years at UBS, the last six as head of its asset management business.
facts.quote: He rejoined Credit Suisse in April 2021 having previously worked at UBS for 11 years, the last six as head of the firm's asset management business.

sources.title: Credit Suisse CEO change: Gottstein out, Körner in, strategic review

facts.claim: On 19 March 2023 the Swiss Federal Council amended its emergency ordinance of 16 March 2023 to add Article 5a, authorising FINMA to order the write-down of Credit Suisse's AT1 capital; FINMA directed the write-down the same day.
facts.quote: the Federal Council amended the emergency ordinance of 16 March 2023 to include a provision (Art. 5a) authorising FINMA to order the write-down of AT1 capital

facts.claim: Roughly CHF 16 billion (one source: about CHF 16.5 billion) of Credit Suisse AT1 bonds were written down to zero as part of the package stabilising Credit Suisse through a merger with UBS, which FINMA said required extraordinary state support.
